---
title: "Business Critical analysis"
description: "The steps to follow when an impact dimension scores Level 4."
---

Business Critical work is registered with the Analytical Quality and Assurance function and assured
at Level 4 BCA. Start at step 1 to find out whether yours is.

## Steps by phase

| Step | Phase | Outputs |
|---|---|---|
| [1. Decide whether it is Business Critical](#step-1-decide-at-scoping-whether-it-is-business-critical) | Phase 1 | The Business Critical answer, recorded yes or no |
| [2. Name who is accountable](#step-2-name-who-is-accountable) | Phase 1 | A named Analysis Senior Responsible Officer |
| [3. Read the assurance level](#step-3-read-the-assurance-level) | Phase 1 | The likelihood scored, and the tool complete |
| [4. Get it on the register](#step-4-get-it-on-the-register) | Phase 1 | The register entry |
| [5. Do the work to Level 4 BCA](#step-5-do-the-work-to-the-enhanced-standard) | Phases 1 to 4 | The eleven documents of the stack, each in the phase the picture gives |
| [6. Say what is uncertain](#step-6-say-what-is-uncertain) | Phase 3 | The uncertainty documented and quantified |
| [7. Publish what was checked and get sign-off](#step-7-publish-what-was-checked) | Phase 4 | The quality assurance statement, published with the output, and the sign-off |
| [8. Set a review date and approve any new use](#step-8-keep-it-true-after-first-use) | Phase 5 | A review date, and approval of any new use |
| [9. Review the work and revalidate the designation](#step-9-review-and-revalidate-the-designation) | Phase 5 | The designation revalidated |

## Step 1. Decide at scoping whether it is Business Critical {#step-1-decide-at-scoping-whether-it-is-business-critical}

{{< include /guidance/_partials/bca-determination.qmd >}}

## Step 2. Name who is accountable {#step-2-name-who-is-accountable}

The commissioner names an Analysis Senior Responsible Officer at scoping, with the Analytical
Quality and Assurance Lead.

- They must be senior enough to carry the risks across the lifecycle.
- They approve the work as fit for purpose before it is used.
- The commissioner may take the role.

::: {.nhsuk-inset-text}
More detail: [the Analysis Senior Responsible Officer role](/guidance/06-roles/analysis-senior-responsible-officer.qmd).
:::

## Step 3. Read the assurance level {#step-3-read-the-assurance-level}

{{< include /guidance/_partials/bca-assurance-level.qmd >}}

## Step 4. Get it on the register {#step-4-get-it-on-the-register}

Log the work with the Analytical Quality and Assurance function, which holds the Business Critical
register. Do this whether or not the work is a model. See
[who to ask](/guidance/09-resources/r3-who-to-ask.qmd) for how to reach the function.

The entry must hold:

- a named officer accountable for it
- a statement of its intended use
- up to date user documentation
- guidance on quality assurance
- confirmation from the accountable officer that it is suitable for its intended use

Give the named officer and the intended use at scoping. Add the user documentation and the
guidance on quality assurance as they are produced, and the officer's confirmation at sign-off.

The accountable officer is the Analysis Senior Responsible Officer named at step 2. For a model,
the requirements below apply across its whole life.

## Step 5. Do the work to Level 4 BCA {#step-5-do-the-work-to-the-enhanced-standard}

Do everything Level 3 Comprehensive requires. Follow the Level 3 checks in
[what your level requires](/guidance/07-deciding-your-assurance-level/what-your-level-requires.qmd#what-each-phase-requires).

Level 4 BCA adds these checks:

- formal audits
- external review
- additional scrutiny of the documentation
- scrutiny of the structural and conceptual assumptions
- additional scenario testing

Check that everyone using and assuring the work has the skills and knowledge for it. Where they do
not, arrange specialist induction or training.

### The documentation stack

Complete the eleven documents below, generally in the order shown. Update an earlier document when a
review shows it needs changing. For an analysis that already exists, review what is there, find the
gaps and fill them first.

[NHSBSA templates and documents](/guidance/09-resources/r2-templates-and-documents.qmd) says where the
Analytical Assurance Decision Tool and the quality assurance appraisal workbook are held. For the
other templates, write to the analytical assurance mailbox in
[who to ask](/guidance/09-resources/r3-who-to-ask.qmd).

The picture shows who owns each document and the phase it belongs to. The table says what each one holds.

{{< include /guidance/_partials/diagram-documents-by-role-and-phase.qmd >}}

| No. | Document | What it holds |
|-----|----------------------|-------------------------------------|
| 1 | Analytical plan | The question, the purpose, why the decision matters, the commissioner and the dates |
| 2 | Scope | The decisions it supports, inputs and outputs, boundaries and limitations, resources and principal risks |
| 3 | Analytical Assurance Decision Tool | Whether the work meets the requirements of Business Critical analysis. Saved and attached to the Specification |
| 4 | Specification | Calculations, assumptions, expected accuracy, and the testing that shows it meets its purpose |
| 5 | Quality assurance plan | The register of assurance actions: owner, priority, progress and target date, tied to the appraisal reference codes |
| 6 | Quality assurance appraisal, basic information | Model name, identifier and contact, and the four named owners: the Analysis Senior Responsible Officer, the Lead Assurer, the analyst and the commissioner |
| 7 | The analysis or model itself | No template. Use the Model Guidance Document. Use what the build and testing show to fill the data, assumptions and risk registers |
| 8 | Technical guide | Enough for someone with no prior knowledge to take over its operation and development |
| 9 | User guide | Enough for a new team member to run it and produce the expected outputs |
| 10 | Quality assurance appraisal, assurance review | Six worksheets scored, with a reason for each rating and the actions it raises |
| 11 | Quality assurance sign-off | The Assurance Report worksheet: what was reviewed, the statement, the risks and the approval |

: The eleven Business Critical documents and what each holds

- Give each action in the quality assurance plan and the assurance review a priority:
  - Must: essential to address a significant risk, issue or control weakness.
  - Should: recommended to improve quality, robustness or assurance.
  - Could: additional benefit, but not needed for the analysis to be acceptable.
- Hold the documentation centrally with the Analytical Quality and Assurance function. You may keep working copies locally.
- Send each new production version of a model to the Analytical Quality and Assurance function when it is released.
- Name each file with the document type first and the analysis second, for example `User_Guide_AnalysisName`.

## Step 6. Say what is uncertain {#step-6-say-what-is-uncertain}

Document the uncertainty. Quantify it wherever the method allows. Quantifying is required at
Level 4 BCA.

Write down any assumption that would change the answer if it were wrong.

::: {.nhsuk-inset-text}
More detail: [what uncertainty is, how to manage it and how to write it up](/guidance/09-resources/r10-uncertainty.qmd).
:::

## Step 7. Publish what was checked and get sign-off {#step-7-publish-what-was-checked}

Publish the quality assurance statement with the output. From Level 3, it carries what
[Phase 4](/guidance/04-delivery-and-sign-off/index.qmd) lists. At Level 4 BCA it also carries:

- the Business Critical register reference
- the Lead Assurer, named, from outside the delivering team
- the Analysis Senior Responsible Officer who approved the work as fit for its intended use
- the quality assurance sign-off reference from the quality assurance appraisal

Get sign-off from the Lead Assurer, then from the Analysis Senior Responsible Officer. Update the
Business Critical register entry when the work is signed off.

## Step 8. Set a review date and approve any new use {#step-8-keep-it-true-after-first-use}

The Analysis Senior Responsible Officer sets a review date with the commissioner, using the cadence
for your level in
[Phase 5, review](/guidance/05-review/index.qmd).

Get the Analysis Senior Responsible Officer to approve any new use before it goes ahead. A new use is
a different purpose, or a change in the context of its use.

Before any reuse, run [the four checks before reuse](/guidance/05-review/index.qmd#check-four-things-before-any-reuse).
If any answer is yes, [score the assurance level again](/guidance/07-deciding-your-assurance-level/index.qmd).

## Step 9. Review the work and revalidate the designation {#step-9-review-and-revalidate-the-designation}

Revalidate the designation as part of the [Phase 5 review](/guidance/05-review/index.qmd). The
Analysis Senior Responsible Officer does this annually, and before any reuse for a new purpose.

Check it in both directions. Work that was Business Critical may no longer be. Work that was not may
have become so as its use widened.

After sign-off, keep assuring the work:

- Check that it is used as intended, with its caveats.
- Log any errors and record any improvements.
- Keep data and assumptions up to date through scheduled reviews.
- After any material change, review the documentation and the assurance requirements, in proportion
  to the change. Check these six documents:
  - the scope
  - the specification
  - the user guide
  - the technical guide
  - the quality assurance appraisal
  - the quality assurance plan
